description: kitsu for Codex: introduces Kitsu's coordination workflow and supporting gate through `kitsu context` at session start, refuses, with the reason, a git call that skips the hooks, a kitsu call that turns the gate off, or a patch of kitsu.toml, a hook file, the git configuration or a record of kitsu, because Codex cannot ask from a hook, and gives `kitsu tokens record` the notice that a role or the session has ended. The commands for sh run kitsu only from an entry of PATH that is an absolute path. The commands for Windows go to the root of the session's drive and then to the Windows folder before they run kitsu, so a relative entry of PATH is read from there and not from the session's directory. Every command exits 0, so an old or missing kitsu blocks nothing. The git hooks decide about commits and pushes; this file does not.

hooks.command: sh -c 'p=; IFS=:; set -f; for d in $PATH; do case "$d" in /*) p="${p:+$p:}$d";; esac; done; unset IFS; set +f; [ -n "$p" ] || exit 0; PATH=$p; c=$(command -v kitsu 2>/dev/null); [ -x "$c" ] || c=; case "$c" in /*) "$c" context --host codex;; *) echo "kitsu is not installed or is missing from absolute PATH. Install it: https://github.com/belevtsev/kitsu#install";; esac; true'
hooks.commandWindows: set NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath=1& cd \& cd /d %SystemRoot% && (kitsu context --host codex 2>nul & if errorlevel 9009 echo kitsu is not installed or is missing from absolute PATH. Install it: https://github.com/belevtsev/kitsu#install) & exit /b 0
